messages:
Priya K: Quick question — thinking about tenant fencing for the quota layer. Current coupling between admission and rate-limiter makes canary rollouts risky.
Luca: +1. we see spikes during canaries when tokens are reclaimed, leads to noisy evictions.
Maggie: Can you sketch the separation you have in mind?
Priya K: Idea: split "fencing" concerns into a thin TenantGuard interface that enforces hard isolation (max qps, reserved burst) and a separate FairScheduler that does soft admission based on weights. TenantGuard is stateless-ish (config + counters) and sits in front of FairScheduler.
Luca: Sounds good. What about fairness across multi-region shards? We need global view for weights.
Priya K: We can keep per-region TenantGuard, and a cross-region aggregator emits smoothed weights. FairScheduler can accept periodic weight updates. If aggregator unavailable, fallback to last-known.
dan: What are the tradeoffs? latency, complexity, correctness?
Priya K: Tradeoffs: + isolation and simpler canaries; - added path for weight sync, slightly increased config surface. We avoid global locks; use eventual consistency for weights.
Maggie: How would this affect eviction ordering? Right now admission decides both admission and eviction priority.
Priya K: Eviction priority will remain part of FairScheduler. TenantGuard only does pass/fail for hard limits. So eviction decisions stay where the fairness policy lives.
sre-bot: Deploy note: last rollout to rate-limiter was 2026-02-14T03:22, no evictions >=P2.
Luca: Any api/interface changes? clients call admission.Check(req) today.
Priya K: New plan: admission.Check(req) returns AdmissionDecision {allowed: bool, reason: string, softTokenCost?: number}. For legacy clients, default softTokenCost == 1. We add a separate endpoint for weight updates.
Maggie: We need metrics: per-tenant hard_denied, soft_denied, fairness_score. Also histograms for latency impact.
Priya K: Agreed. Also add an audit log of fence-trigger events for security/enterprise.
dan: What's the rollout plan?
Priya K: 1) implement TenantGuard in a feature-flagged path; 2) run canaries in staging with synthetic tenants; 3) enable for select customers behind feature flag; 4) gradually flip to global.
Luca: Any DB/state changes? counters persisted in redis currently.
Priya K: We'll keep redis for counters, but change key layout to include fence version. We'll also add a TTL shim to avoid counter leakage.
Maggie: Dev work estimates?
Priya K: ~3 wks for core impl + 1 wk for observability + 1 wk of rollouts and fixes.
Luca: Nits: ensure tenant weights are rate-limited when pushing from aggregator to avoid thundering.
Priya K: yup, use leaky-bucket and versioned weight documents.
Maggie: Can we add a fallback admission policy that lets low-priority tenants in when utilization < 40%?
Priya K: That's a config knob on FairScheduler — willing to add.
dan: Security note: tenant fencing must respect reserved enterprise quotas & KMS-kept config.
Priya K: We'll add an encrypted config flag for enterprise reserved quotas.
sre-bot: Action item created: #INFRA-3124 Implement TenantGuard thin interface (assignee: Priya K).
Luca: Ok let's sync on Tuesday 9am to review proto and key metrics.
Maggie: If someone wants to prototyping the weight aggregator, ping me.
Priya K: thanks all :thumbsup:
